item.title: Brewers rally from four down for a 2-0 World Series lead
item.description: Milwaukee erased a four-run first-inning deficit and beat Tampa Bay 5-4 behind six scoreless bullpen innings. Rookie Cooper Pratt atoned for an early error with the go-ahead single, while Sal Frelick homered to tie the game. The Brewers take a 2-0 Series lead to Florida.

item.title: UCF upsets No. 2 BYU in a chaotic college football Saturday
item.description: UCF stopped BYU in double overtime for the biggest ranked win in program history, while Cincinnati toppled No. 8 Texas Tech and No. 6 Indiana won at Michigan for the first time since 1967. No. 1 Miami, unbeaten UCLA and unbeaten Utah all held serve.

item.title: Rybakina retains Ningbo title and strengthens her No. 1 case
item.description: Elena Rybakina beat Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 6-2 to defend the Ningbo Open title and claim a tour-leading fourth trophy of 2026. The Australian Open and U.S. Open champion moved closer to securing the year-end No. 1 ranking before next month's WTA Finals.

item.title: Bayern says Kompany is stable after training-ground collapse
item.description: Bayern Munich says manager Vincent Kompany remains hospitalized in stable condition after collapsing during reserve-team training. The 40-year-old had been battling a virus and will be sidelined for weeks while doctors determine the cause; assistant Aaron Danks will take charge.

item.title: Brewers survive ninth-inning scare to win World Series opener
item.description: Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 3-2 in Game 1, stranding the tying run at third after replay overturned an apparent game-ending double play. Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run in five innings and opened with a 103.5 mph fastball, the fastest pitch recorded in World Series history.

item.title: Leclerc leads U.S. Grand Prix practice as Antonelli nears history
item.description: Charles Leclerc topped both Friday practice sessions in Austin, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli just 0.042 seconds behind in the second. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver can become Formula One's youngest champion on Sunday if he wins and other results fall his way.

item.title: Olympic marathon champion Jepchirchir suspended after EPO finding
item.description: Former Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been provisionally suspended after an out-of-competition sample tested positive for EPO. The 33-year-old Kenyan, a four-time World Marathon Majors winner, gave the sample before winning the Sydney Marathon.

item.title: Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's diagnosis
item.description: Pro Football Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk says he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease about 18 months ago after noticing persistent hand stiffness. The 53-year-old Southern coach says medication has helped him maintain normal activities, and he shared the news to encourage others to get possible symptoms checked early.

item.title: Rays delay Rasmussen and give Martinez the World Series opener
item.description: In a significant change from the World Series matchup announced Thursday, Tampa Bay will start Nick Martinez in Game 1 and give ace Drew Rasmussen extra rest. Martinez led the Rays with 180 innings and a 3.10 ERA; Rasmussen is 2-0 with a 1.29 postseason ERA.

item.title: Brewers and Rays meet with a first World Series title guaranteed
item.description: For the first time since 1980, the World Series matches two franchises that have never won it. Milwaukee brings a club-record 103 wins and its first pennant since 1982; Tampa Bay returns after a comeback ALCS. Game 1 on Friday pairs two of MLB's smaller-market, lower-payroll clubs.

item.title: Doncic and Kessler launch the post-LeBron Lakers with a rout
item.description: Los Angeles opened its first season after LeBron James with a 127-105 win over Golden State. Luka Doncic had 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists, while newcomer Walker Kessler scored 26 on 12-for-12 shooting as the Lakers built a 35-point lead.

item.title: 2027 Tours reward time trialists and return to Britain
item.description: The 2027 men's Tour de France will start in Edinburgh and include 71 kilometers of individual time trials, the most since 2012. The Tour de France Femmes begins in Leeds with a London team time trial and finishes atop the Puy de Dome.

item.title: England's football regulator says it can force club owners to sell
item.description: Independent Football Regulator chair David Kogan says the new body can remove owners who fail its fitness and propriety tests. It may examine Manchester City after the club's appeal over 114 Premier League financial-rule breaches, and it also wants more money flowing to lower-division clubs.

item.title: LeBron's Philadelphia debut spoils the Knicks' banner night
item.description: LeBron James began his record-extending 24th NBA season with 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists as Philadelphia beat defending champion New York 106-100. Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 28 points, quieting Madison Square Garden after the Knicks received rings and raised their first title banner in 53 years.

item.title: Celebrini scores twice as Sharks erase two-goal deficit
item.description: Macklin Celebrini scored the opening goal and the overtime winner as San Jose rallied past Montreal 4-3. Michael Misa and Tyler Toffoli erased a 3-1 third-period deficit before Celebrini converted Ivar Stenberg's no-look pass on a power play 2:13 into overtime.
